title: Endodontic Instruments & Rubber Dam Isolation — Test

mcqs.q: A file is best defined as:
opts: A tapered, pointed metal instrument with cutting edges that enlarges the canal
A blunt instrument used to condense gutta-percha
A rubber device used to isolate the tooth
A hand instrument used only to remove pulp tissue
mcqs.explain: Files are classified principally by activation method, alloy, cross-sectional shape, taper and tip design.

mcqs.q: In an ENGINE-DRIVEN file, the part that replaces the handle and is placed inside the handpiece is the:
mcqs.explain: Engine-driven files have a shank that seats in the handpiece, plus the rubber stopper, shaft, working part, tip and measuring lines.

mcqs.q: The two main functions of the file tip are to:
opts: Guide the file through the canal and aid deeper penetration
Measure the working length and seal the apex
Condense and compact the filling material
mcqs.explain: The tip guides the instrument and helps it penetrate deeper; its configuration strongly affects shaping ability.

mcqs.q: Compared with a conventional cutting tip, a modified NON-cutting tip:
opts: Maintains the original canal curvature better
Cannot be used in rotary instruments
mcqs.explain: Non-cutting (modified) tips are better at maintaining the original curvature of the canal.

mcqs.q: A clinician unfamiliar with the tip design of a rotary instrument risks:
opts: Transporting the canal or generating excessive torsion and breaking the file
mcqs.explain: An enlarging tip held too long in one position in a curved canal transports the canal; excessive torsion fractures the file.

mcqs.q: The flute of a file is the:
opts: Groove in the working surface that collects soft tissue and dentine chips
Angle between the cutting edge and long axis
Metal core at the centre of the file
mcqs.explain: The flute collects debris; the surface of greatest diameter following the groove forms the cutting edge (blade).

mcqs.q: Which is NOT a function of the radial land?
opts: Increases the chip space of the instrument
Reduces the tendency of the file to thread into the canal
Centres the instrument in the canal space
mcqs.explain: The radial land reduces threading, supports the cutting edge and centres the file — it forms a larger contact area, which does not increase chip space.

mcqs.q: An instrument with a helical angle of LESS than 45° (reamers, K-files) works most efficiently with a:
mcqs.explain: Helical angle <45° (reamers, K-files) requires a rotary reaming motion; >45° (Hedström) requires a filing motion.

mcqs.q: The greater the chip space of an instrument, the:
opts: More efficiently it transports debris and the more flexible it is
Less efficient it is at removing dentine
mcqs.explain: Chip space = canal lumen area minus instrument cross-sectional area. More chip space means better debris transport, a smaller cross-section and greater flexibility.

mcqs.q: A POSITIVE rake angle (>10°) produces a cutting action and is characteristic of:
mcqs.explain: H-files have a positive rake angle (cutting action); reamers, K-files and rotary NiTi have negative rake angles (scraping).

mcqs.q: A NEGATIVE rake angle results in a:
mcqs.explain: Negative rake angle (<10°) scrapes; all instruments requiring a rotary reaming motion have a negative rake angle.

mcqs.q: The diameter of a file at the tip, from which it derives its number and colour code, is designated:
mcqs.explain: D0 is the cross-sectional diameter at the first rake angle (the tip); D16 is 16 mm coronal and is the largest diameter.

mcqs.q: The tip diameter of a size #50 file is:
mcqs.explain: Divide the file number by 100: #10 = 0.1 mm, #50 = 0.5 mm, #100 = 1 mm at D0.

mcqs.q: What is the diameter at D16 of a 40/.02 instrument?
What is the diameter of a size-20 rotary file with a constant 6% taper, 3 mm from the tip?
ISO-normed files are available in 21, 25 and 31 mm, but ALL of them share:
opts: A 16 mm section of cutting flutes
mcqs.explain: Regardless of overall length, every ISO file has a 16 mm long cutting-flute section.

mcqs.q: Which instrument lengths are most commonly selected for molars?
mcqs.explain: 18/21 mm for molars, 25 mm for anteriors, 28/31 mm for canines.

mcqs.q: ISO instrument numbering increases by:
opts: 5 units up to size 60, then 10 units up to size 100
mcqs.explain: Numbering runs 10–100, increasing by 5 up to 60 then by 10 to 100; the range was revised to include 6–140.

mcqs.q: Which colour corresponds to an ISO size 30 file?
mcqs.explain: The repeating colour code is white 15, yellow 20, red 25, blue 30, green 35, black 40 (then repeating for 45–80 and 90–140).

mcqs.q: All ISO-sized HAND instruments have a constant taper of:
mcqs.explain: Every mm of the cutting part increases by 0.02 mm — 0.32 mm over the 16 mm blade. Rotary NiTi with other tapers is not ISO sized.

mcqs.q: The K-file is manufactured by:
opts: Twisting and pulling a stainless-steel wire of rectangular/triangular cross-section
Casting molten NiTi in a mould
mcqs.explain: Twisting increases resistance to torsion and flexion, making the K-file useful for initial canal negotiation.

mcqs.q: An advantage of the K-file over the H-file is that it:
opts: Is more flexible with less chance of canal transportation
Can only be used in a rotary handpiece
mcqs.explain: K-files are more flexible and transport the canal less, but have less cutting efficiency and may extrude debris periapically.

mcqs.q: The H-file (Hedström) is manufactured by grinding a round wire and therefore:
opts: Has a positive rake angle and cuts only on the pull stroke
Has a negative rake angle and cuts in both directions
Is the most flexible hand file
mcqs.explain: The H-file has a positive rake angle (cutting action) and cuts on the pull stroke only — it is popular for circumferential filing.

mcqs.q: Why must an H-file NOT be rotated inside the canal?
opts: Deep grinding reduces its central metal mass, so it may engage and separate
It would polish rather than cut
It would over-enlarge the orifice only
mcqs.explain: Because of deep grinding and reduced central mass of metal, rotating an H-file risks engagement and fracture; it is not recommended in narrow or curved canals.

mcqs.q: Which file is specifically designed for calcified canals and for creating a glide path?
mcqs.explain: The C/C+ file is stainless steel with an extra-stiff construction, available in 21 and 25 mm, ideal for calcified canals.

mcqs.q: A barbed broach is primarily used to:
opts: Remove pulp tissue or easily engaged materials from the canal
Enlarge and shape the canal walls
mcqs.explain: It is thin, flexible and fragile with sharp backward/obliquely curving projections; it may break if engaged, so it is avoided in narrow canals.

mcqs.q: Watch winding is described as:
opts: Reciprocating back-and-forth rotation in about a 30° arc with light apical pressure
A 90° rotation followed by a pull
mcqs.explain: Watch winding uses small K- and C-files for initial penetration and negotiating canals.

mcqs.q: Reaming is defined as:
opts: Clockwise cutting rotation of 180–360°, then pulling coronally to remove dentine cuts
mcqs.explain: Reaming planes the walls and enlarges the canal; it is used with K- and C-files.

mcqs.q: In the quarter-turn pull technique, the file is placed to the point of binding and then:
opts: Rotated 90° and pulled along the canal wall
mcqs.explain: It is a modification of filing: place to binding, rotate 90°, then pull the instrument along the canal wall.

mcqs.q: Regarding isolation in endodontics, the rule is:
opts: Isolation is optional if the patient cooperates
Multiple-tooth isolation for anterior teeth only
mcqs.explain: Endodontics always uses single-tooth rubber dam isolation, with the dam edge everted (and sealant if needed) for a perfect seal.

mcqs.q: Which is an ACCESSORY (not a main component) of the rubber dam kit?
mcqs.explain: Main components: sheet, punch, clamps, forceps, frame. Accessories: dental floss, wedge, OraSeal, Liquidam and Teflon.

mcqs.q: Flossing around the bow of the clamp is advised mainly to:
opts: Retrieve the clamp safely if it slips or fractures
Improve the seal of the dam
mcqs.explain: The floss provides a safety tie — especially when checking the fit of the clamp without the sheet in place. Aspiration/swallowing safety.

saqs.q: Name the components of an endodontic hand file and state how an engine-driven file differs.
saqs.a: Hand file: handle, rubber stopper, shaft, working part, tip. An engine-driven file replaces the handle with a shank that sits in the handpiece, and adds measuring lines.

head: Hand file
Engine-driven file
rows: HANDLE — held by the fingers; carries the number, colour and shape
SHANK — placed inside the handpiece, and carries measuring lines
Shaft — between handle and working part
Working part — bears the cutting surface

saqs.q: Describe the longitudinal and cross-sectional design features of endodontic instruments.
saqs.a: Flute — collects debris. Cutting edge — surface of greatest diameter. Radial land — flat between flutes, centres the file. Helical angle — <45° reaming (K-file), >45° filing (H-file). Chip space — more space, better debris transport. Rake angle — negative (<10°) scrapes, positive (>10°) cuts.

the angle the cutting edge makes with the long axis. <45° (reamers, K-files) → rotary reaming; >45° (Hedström) → filing
canal lumen area minus the instrument's cross-section — more chip space means better debris transport and greater flexibility
angle between the cutting edge and the surface cut. Negative (<10°) → scraping (reamers, K-files, rotary NiTi); positive (>10°) → cutting (H-files)

saqs.q: Explain the ISO standardization of endodontic files (length, D-points, numbering, colour and taper).
saqs.a: Length: 21, 25, 31 mm, all with a 16 mm flute section. D-points: D0 at the tip to D16. Numbering: tip diameter in hundredths of a mm (#50 = 0.5 mm), 10–100 in steps of 5 to 60 then 10. Colour repeats every six sizes. Taper: constant .02 (2%) for all ISO hand files.

saqs.q: Compare the K-file and the H-file (manufacture, rake angle, motion, advantages and disadvantages).
saqs.a: K-file: twisted wire, negative rake, scrapes, cuts both ways, used watch-winding/filing/reaming, can be pre-curved. More flexible, less transportation; but less cutting efficiency and extrudes debris. H-file: ground wire, positive rake, cuts on the pull stroke only, must not be rotated. Better cutting and pushes debris coronally; but inflexible, fractures and is aggressive.

saqs.q: Describe the three manipulation motions used with endodontic hand instruments.
saqs.a: Watch winding — back-and-forth ~30° with light apical pressure, for initial penetration. Reaming — clockwise 180–360° to plane and enlarge, then pull coronally. Filing — push-pull, pressing laterally on withdrawal; the quarter-turn pull is a modification.

head: Motion
What it is and when
rows: reciprocating back-and-forth rotation through about a 30° arc with light apical pressure — small K- and C-files, for initial penetration, negotiating canals and working files to place
clockwise cutting rotation of 180–360° that planes the walls and enlarges the canal; the file is then pulled coronally to remove the dentine cuts — K- and C-files
push-pull, pressing the file laterally while withdrawing it to plane the wall — best with H-files and K-files. The quarter-turn pull is a modification: place to binding, rotate 90°, then pull

saqs.q: List the components of the rubber dam kit and state the rules for isolation in endodontics.
saqs.a: Kit: sheet, punch, clamps, forceps, frame; accessories floss, wedge, OraSeal, Liquidam, Teflon. Rules: isolate a SINGLE tooth always; invert the dam edge for a seal and use sealant on a leaking edge; tie floss to the clamp bow against aspiration or swallowing.

list: Accessories — dental floss, wedge, OraSeal, Liquidam, Teflon
In endodontics isolation is ALWAYS of a single tooth
Invert/evert the dam edge around the tooth to obtain a seal; apply sealant around a broken or leaking edge
Tie floss around the bow of the clamp — at least when checking the fit without the sheet — against aspiration or swallowing
